guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.guide.spr:
The forest spreads by spores. Spores from the forest ride the wind, settle on the ground and sprout there, turning the land into new forest.

■Where spores come from
Land that has become forest keeps releasing spores, and the deeper the forest, the more it releases. The crowns of giant trees release spores all day, most of all in the morning. The corpses of creatures consumed by spores and rooted Sproutlings release spores too. When the earth splits open, a flood of spores bursts from the rift and rains down on the land around it all at once.

■Riding the wind
There is a single wind for the whole world, blowing the same way everywhere. It turns slowly and shifts sharply when rain begins. Spores are carried downwind, and even without wind they seep slowly into the surroundings. Thunderstorms become spore storms: clumps of spores are lifted high into the sky and may come down hundreds of blocks away. A Wind Vane shows which way the wind is coming from.

■Settling
Spores settle on the ground at night and after rain, showing as dust on the ground and leaves. The right needle of the Spore Density Meter shows how much has settled. Right-click the dust with a shovel to sweep it away (the settled spores there drop a little, and you get spores).

■Sprouting
When enough spores have settled and the ground is moist, the land sprouts. A Sproutling appears where it sprouts, walks to a moist spot and puts down roots, then spreads its roots and corrupts the ground around it. A rooted Sproutling can be broken by hand. The forest spreads underwater and into the sea as well.

■Stages of the forest
Sprouted land is swallowed by the forest in three stages. It never goes back on its own.
- Freshly sprouted: land that has just sprouted.
- Overgrown: about 2 days after sprouting. From here on it is forest. The more the forest spreads, the further the phases advance.
- Engulfed: the forest's final form after a long time (see "Engulfed" in the Biomes chapter).

The forest also spreads into land where no player is. If you turn off "Spread into unloaded areas" in the world settings, sprouting waits until someone comes near.

■Holding it back
While running, a Spore Purifier draws in the spores around it and keeps them from sprouting. Defeating a giant tree's Hive Node stops the nearby giant trees from releasing spores.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.mob.title: Mobs
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.sp:
You catch it by breathing spores on corrupted land or when forest creatures attack you.

■Players
There are 10 stages. It worsens by one stage every 10 minutes; each new stage hurts you a little and lowers your maximum health by 1 until you are cured.
- From stage 1: you get hungry faster (more at higher stages)
- From stage 2: forest creatures notice you from farther away (up to 20 blocks)
- From stage 4: lower armor (up to 20%%)
- From stage 8: lower attack damage (up to 15%%)
- While infected: experience is drained every 10 seconds

10 minutes after stage 10, the spores consume you and a blight fern sprouts where you fell. Milk does not cure it. A Spore-Stopping Elixir, made in a mortar, lowers it by one stage.

■Other creatures
Animals and villagers can catch it too. If it runs out uncured, they fall, leaving a corrupted corpse or a blight fern.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.cl:
You get this under the spore canopy spread by a Sporophyll (G4). It lasts 30 seconds after you leave the canopy.
- You move slower
- Your attack weakens
- G4 creatures notice you from 24 blocks farther away

It vanishes as soon as you enter the range of a Spore Purifier. If you get caught under a Sporophyll's canopy, fall back to a purifier.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.ph:
You get this when a Phyllosens (G4) spots you. It means the forest creatures have been told where you are.

While you have it, creatures with Phyllosens' Guidance come for you however far away you are, even through walls.

It keeps renewing while you are near the Phyllosens (32 blocks) and fades 1 minute after you leave. While a Phyllosens is searching for prey, it can spot you from much farther. When the icon is gone, you are no longer being hunted.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.sp:
Spores a Sporophyll (G4) gives to forest creatures under its canopy. Their attacks:
- ignore 20%% of your armor
- wear down your armor's durability by as much as the damage dealt

It lasts 1 minute after they leave the canopy and vanishes inside a Spore Purifier's range. Avoid fighting under a Sporophyll's canopy.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.ph:
A mark a Phyllosens (G4) gives to nearby forest creatures. Creatures with it know where players with Phyllosens' Gaze are and attack them regardless of distance or walls.

It lasts 1 minute. Once the Phyllosens is dead, no new marks are given out.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.wa:
Rot that forest creatures (G1-G10) get after staying in water for 30 seconds. It continues while they are in water and lingers 30 seconds after they leave it, dealing 1 damage every second.

Forest creatures that live in seas and rivers are immune.

Holding them back with moats and channels wears them down.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.we:
You get this from eating a Ripe Hanging Vine Glow Fruit. While it lasts, running and jumping do not make you hungry. It lasts 30 seconds.

A Large Undeveloped Fruit makes it last 3 minutes, but worsens Spore Infection by one stage.

Both also give Savory Scent, so forest creatures notice you more easily.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.sa:
You get this from eating a Ripe Hanging Vine Glow Fruit, an Undeveloped Seed or a Large Undeveloped Fruit. A savory smell rises from you, and forest creatures (G1-G10) notice you from 15 blocks farther away. Ordinary creatures do not care.

It lasts 1 minute from the glow fruit, 5 seconds from the seed and 5 minutes from the large fruit.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.biome.jun:
The most common kind of forest. Undergrowth thrives on moss-covered ground among overgrown trees. Saplings sometimes grow into towering giant trees.

Wood from corrupted land (overgrown logs and planks) works just like ordinary wood.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.biome.swa:
A forest full of water. In the overgrowth stage puddles form; once overgrown, flat ground gets ponds and narrow channels, and slopes are cut into terraces with waterfalls dropping from step to step. Ground at the water's edge turns to mud.

The original trees fall over or rot away. Because the ground itself is reshaped, your footing may sink under water in land that becomes swamp.

Faintly glowing spore sacs grow in its caves.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.biome.fun:
A watery forest like the swamp, but scattered fungal pillars stand in place of trees. Puddles, ponds and channels form just as in the swamp.

In its caves, fungal pillars join ceiling and floor, huge fungal caps jut from the walls, and glowing mycelium is mixed in here and there.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.biome.wat:
Seas and rivers are corrupted too. Whatever the forest type, they become corrupted seas and rivers, covered in moss and water plants down to the bottom.

Most forest creatures get Water Rot from staying in water too long. Those that live in seas and rivers are fine.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.biome.cli:
The final form of a forest that has stayed overgrown for a long time. It starts to appear from Phase 5. Land widely surrounded by overgrown forest becomes engulfed, oldest first.

In the engulfed forest the canopy swallows the light; even under a bright sky the forest floor stays dim. Underground, everything down to bedrock is replaced with forest blocks.

Glowing ley veins run underground, and engulfed ores lie there too. Burning cannot undo it.

Swamps, fungal swamps, seas and rivers each have their own engulfed form.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.biome.cry:
When jungle becomes engulfed, about one region in four turns into a crystal field, with pillars of energy crystals standing among the trees.

The crystals glow faintly and mark the way in the dark engulfed forest.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.biome.net:
When the forest reaches the frame of a lit Nether portal, corruption starts on the other side too. If the forest in the Nether reaches another portal, it can come back to the Overworld from there.

Each of the Nether's five landscapes goes through overgrowth and overgrown:
- Nether Wastes
- Crimson Forest
- Warped Forest
- Soul Sand Valley
- Basalt Deltas

Grass grows on netherrack, and flowing lava is hardened into basalt from its source. Piglins and others stop spawning. The Nether has no engulfed stage.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.biome.end:
If the forest reaches the End portal before any player does, the End's main island is entirely covered in plants. By the time you enter, it is already a forest island.

The End forest has only one kind and no stages. The obsidian pillars, End crystals and exit portal stay as they are. The outer islands are not covered.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.biome.bur:
What is left after burning the forest with a flamethrower. Burn the land until less than half the ground is corrupted, and it leaves the forest and becomes burnt wasteland.

While it is burnt, corruption cannot enter. After 3 in-game days it returns to its original landscape.

Engulfed forest does not recover when burnt. The flamethrower is unlocked by the "Purification" research and burns coal or charcoal.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.sp: Lasts 2 minutes after taking Sporeward Powder. Where spore density is 50%% or higher, the time before you catch Spore Infection grows from 30 to 60 seconds.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.al: Lasts 2 minutes after taking Smelling Salts. Holds back the symptoms of Spore Infection (hunger, being noticed, lower armor and attack) without curing it. Maximum health does not return.
guidebook.overgrown_vegetation.effect.st: Lasts 3 minutes after taking a Stasis Pill. Meanwhile, Spore Infection does not worsen.
Lasts 10 minutes after taking a Warmbloom Pill. The next time Spore Infection worsens, it blocks the damage and the loss of maximum health once, then fades.
